bullets.title: Meta AI capex explodes to 14GW by 2027, stock surges 7%+ on compute monetization thesis
bullets.body: Meta's 'Watermelon' model requires an order-of-magnitude more compute than prior generations, with the company planning to double capacity to 14GW next year (from 7GW in 2026). KeyBanc raises PT to $790 (bull case $1,065) on new AI revenue streams; Mizuho initiates Buy on third-party cloud monetization potential at $50B+ per GW. Multiple sell-side analysts note META capex tracking toward $250B in 2027 vs. prior $175-225B estimates, but AI infrastructure economics (Muse Spark API, developer model pricing at $1.25/$4.25 per M tokens) and compute rental revenue justify it. Muse Spark 1.1 reviewed as matching or exceeding Anthropic/OpenAI frontier models at 25% lower cost.

bullets.title: Fed semi-annual report: inflation elevated, driven by tariffs, Middle East, and AI chip prices; hawkish tone dominates
bullets.body: The Fed's semi-annual monetary policy report under Chair Warsh cites tariffs, Iran war, and AI-related chip/memory prices as key inflation drivers. Goldman Sachs estimates AI-induced increases in memory, software, and electricity prices are already adding >0.2% to core PCE YoY, rising to ~0.5% by year-end. 22V Research sets core PCE 0.21% m/m as the hinge: hot prints (>0.30%) push yields higher and pressure risk factors; benign prints support Growth/GARP factors. Prediction markets now price ~67% odds of a September Fed hike.

bullets.title: US 30-year bond yield hits highest since 2007 at 5.058%; term premium expands
bullets.body: The 30-year Treasury auction drew a 5.058% yield, the highest since the pre-GFC period. 10-year yields ended the week near 4.57%. JPMorgan sees 5-year/30-year curve at ~78-82bp resistance and recommends flatteners; 22V Research says 10-year fair value is ~4.5% and higher yields reflect neutral-rate repricing rather than restrictive policy, framing them as less threatening to equities than feared at these levels.

bullets.title: S&P 500 within 0.5% of all-time high; positive gamma dominates short-term options tape
bullets.body: The S&P 500 is 0.5% below an all-time high as of Friday afternoon. SPY options show a $3.5B call wall at the 755 strike with billions of positive gamma; vol-control funds face $12-15B in net buying requirements as 1-month vol falls through mid-July. SPX implied vol fell to 10% for next week (8% for Monday), and term structure is at its lowest point in 90+ days—market is priced for near-perfect outcomes heading into CPI week.

bullets.title: AI debt cycle accelerating: AI firms double 2025 bond sales, Amazon raises $25B, hyperscaler capex tracking $750B+
bullets.body: AI-related IG bond issuance has already surpassed all of 2025's volume. Amazon priced a $25B 8-tranche deal this week; total hyperscaler 144A AI project finance across five transactions reached $53B YTD. JPMorgan credit team downgraded MSFT and META on heavy capex funding needs while upgrading ORCL. Semianalysis forecasts $7T in AI debt outstanding by 2029. BofA flags 'net hiking' central banks as a headwind to equities despite durable FCF trends.

bullets.title: Memory supercycle intact: SK Hynix ADR opens +14-16% on $26.5B record offering; CEO warns shortage persists past 2030
bullets.body: SK Hynix priced its Nasdaq ADR at $149/share, raising $26.5B—the largest-ever US equity offering by a foreign company, surpassing Alibaba's 2014 record. The ADR opened at $170 and traded up to $177 on 69M+ shares. SK Hynix CEO said memory chip shortage may persist past 2030; the SK Group chairman signaled openness to US-based manufacturing and described supply as insufficient even if production doubles over five years. UBS models DRAM industry undersupplied through at least 2Q28.

bullets.title: Goldman/PSC/Morgan Stanley: AI-driven inflation adding 0.2-0.5% to core PCE; memory prices key upside risk into CPI week
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs research quantifies AI-related inflation adding >0.2% to YoY core PCE currently, projected to reach 0.5% by year-end from higher memory, software, and electricity prices. PSC Macro expects headline CPI -0.1% m/m in June on lower energy; core 0.2% m/m vs. 0.3% consensus. MS forecast core CPI +0.22% m/m, 2.8% y/y. Jefferies' inflation framework flags the shift from cost-led to potential demand-led inflation if the Fed eases prematurely. The upcoming CPI/PPI prints (July 14/16) are the key next catalyst for AI theme stocks and rates direction.

bullets.title: US-Iran ceasefire effectively over; Strait of Hormuz disrupted; oil volatile but contained at $72-77
bullets.body: Trump declared the ceasefire with Iran 'over' on Friday, though talks continue via Qatar. US aircraft carriers Lincoln and Bush are positioned near the Iranian coast. Iran's IRGC struck ships near the Strait of Hormuz and US military sites in Bahrain and Kuwait. Hormuz transit averaged 13 ships/day (vs. 10 inbound), with 72% of outbound oil on VLCCs. IEA warns escalation could upend its oil surplus forecast; Goldman flags Middle East disruption could delay supply recovery. WTI has traded in the $68-80 range; markets have largely priced in the conflict as manageable.

bullets.title: Momentum unwind deepens: SOX down 11% in two days post-Samsung; Price Momentum factor at worst drawdown outside recession since 2004
bullets.body: Samsung's record 19x profit surge paradoxically triggered an 11% two-day SOX selloff as the 'buy the news, sell the fact' unwind hit a crowded long. The GS Momentum Pair had its worst 5-day selloff since COVID. Morgan Stanley's MSZZMOMO factor fell 23% from its June 23 peak in just 10 trading days—equaling only the February 2021 meme-stock episode in speed. JPM notes the selloff is positioning-driven, not fundamental: earnings estimates for semis were revised up 20-40% over prior two seasons. Key catalysts for reversal: ASML (July 15) and TSMC (July 16) earnings.

bullets.title: NVDA: multiple macro tailwinds but Kyber/NVL144 rack delayed to 2028 on PCB design issue
bullets.body: NVDA CEO Jensen Huang's NDR meetings described accelerating growth across AI labs, hyperscalers, and enterprise/sovereign segments, with GPU rental rates up 5-10% July YTD. However, SemiAnalysis reported the Kyber NVL144 rack system has been pushed back to 2028 due to PCB midplane manufacturability challenges (NVDA denied the report). Vera Rubin Ultra roadmap is confirmed on track. Morgan Stanley reiterates Overweight/Top Pick, noting NVDA trades at its lowest forward P/E in 10 years, ~10% below the S&P 500 multiple.

bullets.title: NFLX engagement declining: exploring live TV channels, Peacock bundles, and 2030/2034 World Cup bids to stabilize
bullets.body: Multiple brokers and reports flag Netflix's engagement growth at only +2% YoY despite all-time high internal quality metrics in 1Q26. Share of US TV viewership fell to 7.8% in April, the lowest since May 2025. Netflix is exploring always-on live channels (continuous genre/franchise streaming), Peacock bundling in its main app, and bids on 2030/2034 FIFA World Cup rights. JPMorgan maintains Overweight at $118 PT; Citi cuts PT to $100 from $115 on multiple compression. 2Q26 results due July 16.

bullets.title: EM capital flight accelerates: Korea posts record $30.5B non-resident equity outflows (26-year high); EM Asia -$40.5B in June
bullets.body: IIF data shows non-resident investors pulled $30.5B from Korean equities in June—the highest outflow in 26 years—amid SK Hynix ADR-related rotation and broader AI momentum de-grossing. EM Asia saw $40.5B in equity outflows, wiping out gains in other regions. China separately saw a $14B equity outflow in June vs. $8.1B inflow in May. However, Taiwan semiconductor exports surged 43.9% YoY to $133B in 1H26 with DRAM shipments up 158.5%, showing the supply chain is booming even as financial flows reverse.

bullets.title: Japan GPIF/pension reform: Finance Minister pushes domestic allocation shift; yen surges, JGB yields fall 10bp
bullets.body: Japan's Finance Minister Katayama urged GPIF and households to increase domestic asset allocations, triggering a 9bp fall in 10-year JGB yields to 2.77% and a sharp yen appreciation (USD/JPY briefly to 160-161 range). Japanese PPI hit 7.1% YoY in June, the fastest since early 2023, supporting the case for BOJ tightening (markets price 84% odds of another hike by year-end to 1.25%). This represents a meaningful cross-asset macro shift: foreign carry trades and Japanese bond holdings could see structural unwinding.

bullets.title: Broadcom-Apple $30B+ multiyear chip deal through 2031 expands to include custom AI silicon
bullets.body: Apple and Broadcom announced a new agreement exceeding $30B through 2031, covering custom silicon, RF components, and wireless connectivity—producing 15B+ US-made chips. The deal includes a $1.5B capex expansion of AVGO's Fort Collins facility and explicitly adds custom ASIC/AI datacenter XPU work. This removes risk of AVGO losing RF share to QRVO/SWKS and sets a path toward multi-billion AVGO Apple AI revenues by 2029/2030. AVGO shares gained ~4.8% on the announcement.

bullets.title: Data center construction pipeline at 338 GW but build pace implies 12-year clearance; slowing construction growth noted
bullets.body: Data center construction growth has slowed considerably, according to multiple sell-side trackers. Multiple sources note the construction pipeline would take 12 years to clear at the current build rate (338 GW total), up from 10 years previously. This is a counternarrative to the AI capex acceleration story: while demand intent is strong, actual build rates are gated by skilled labor shortages, permitting, power interconnection (ERCOT Batch Zero process), and materials.

bullets.title: China AI capex forecast raised 23% to $1T cumulative through 2030; WAIC July 17 with Huawei 8K-GPU server launch
bullets.body: Jefferies raised China AI capex estimates by 23% to $1T for 2026-30E on better-than-expected chip procurement (300K H200 chips in 2026, Huawei Ascend 950 die-shrink boosting yield from 74 to 137/wafer). The World AI Conference (July 17-20) will feature 1,100+ companies and the launch of Huawei's 8,192-GPU super-node server vs. the current 384-GPU model. DeepSeek is simultaneously developing its own inference chip to reduce Nvidia/Huawei reliance. US allows UAE advanced computing imports without licenses as another export-control shift.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler capex divergence: GOOGL Cloud revenue to exceed $300B by 2028; MSFT replacing OpenAI/Anthropic with in-house MAI models
bullets.body: KeyBanc raises GOOGL PT to $445, modeling Cloud revenue of $102B (2026), $171B (2027), $239B (2028). Separately, Bloomberg reported Microsoft is routing some Excel and Outlook AI prompts to its proprietary MAI models to reduce cost exposure to OpenAI/Anthropic APIs—a signal of the shift from external to internal AI at enterprise scale. Citi CIO survey shows IT budgets growing 3.3% NTM with AI as #1 priority; MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL are the top vendors CIOs plan to increase AI spend on.

bullets.title: Fed Warsh task forces signal regime shift: hawkish inflation focus, AI productivity study, balance sheet review
bullets.body: Chair Warsh assembled five expert task forces on communications, balance sheet policy, real-time data, AI/productivity, and inflation frameworks. The inflation frameworks group leans hawkish with a supply-side focus and may recommend broader inflation measures or nominal income targeting. Governor Waller's inflation-centric language has 'completely flipped' risks from labor to prices. Multiple brokers flag this as a structural shift away from the 2020-2024 framework and toward potential further tightening if core PCE stays above 3.3%.

bullets.title: AI token price war intensifying: META Muse Spark 1.1 at $1.25/M, xAI Grok 4.5 at $2/M vs Anthropic Fable 5 at $10/M
bullets.body: A three-way frontier model pricing battle has emerged: META's Muse Spark 1.1 at $1.25/$4.25 per M input/output tokens; xAI's Grok 4.5 at $2/$6 with 4.2x token efficiency vs Opus; OpenAI GPT-5.6 at $5/$30 but 54% more token-efficient on agentic coding. Anthropic's Fable 5 is at $10/$50. Multiple brokers note this compression is directly impacting OpenAI's revenue trajectory while driving enterprise AI token consumption higher. The trend shifts value from model providers toward infrastructure (NVDA, MU) and toward orchestration platforms.

bullets.title: UBS market fragility index hits all-time high; retail investors showing waning conviction; margin debt at 4.1% of GDP
bullets.body: UBS proprietary market fragility index hit an all-time high, signaling elevated systemic risk. Separately, Bloomberg reports retail traders—who have been among the strongest equity supporters this decade—are showing early signs of waning conviction. Margin debt has risen to approximately 4.1% of GDP, embedding significant leverage in household equity exposure. US household stock ownership is at a record high, with equities now exceeding real estate as a share of net worth.
